author: pereanub
title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - stale onednn_third-party-programs.txt blocks Expand-Archive -Force cleanup
signature: remove item cannot find path because it does not exist pathnotfound removeitemcommand expand archive force|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails with PowerShell Remove-Item PathNotFound error during Expand-Archive -Force

key_errors: Remove-Item : Cannot find path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\licenses\onednn_third-party-programs.txt' because it does not exist.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive with -Force against the pre-existing 'install' directory on a persistent self-hosted Windows runner. PowerShell's -Force implementation first enumerates items it previously extracted into the destination (tracked internally) and tries to Remove-Item them before re-expanding, so it can overwrite them. One of those tracked items, licenses\onednn_third-party-programs.txt, had already been removed or never materialized identically from a prior job/run on the same stateful runner (e.g., a partial cleanup, a race with a concurrent step, or leftover state from a previous job that used a different package layout). When Expand-Archive tries to Remove-Item a path that no longer exists, it throws a non-terminating PathNotFound error that nonetheless causes PowerShell to exit 1, failing the step before any files are actually extracted. This is a runner state/hygiene issue, not a code defect in the PR: the PR's changed files (NPU plugin property handling) have no relationship to packaging, licensing, or the Windows GPU unit test extraction step.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible outside the specific self-hosted Windows ('ptl') runner's stale workspace. To reproduce: on a persistent self-hosted Windows runner with a leftover 'install' directory from a prior build, run `Expand-Archive <pkg>.zip -DestinationPath <install-dir> -Force` after manually deleting one file under install\licenses that Expand-Archive previously extracted; observe the Remove-Item PathNotFound error.
recommended_actions: Clean the self-hosted runner's workspace ('install' directory) before extraction, e.g. `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $INSTALL_DIR` prior to Expand-Archive, instead of relying on -Force to reconcile stale state.

Wrap the Extract OpenVINO packages step with a retry-on-transient-failure mechanism, or catch/ignore PathNotFound errors from the implicit Remove-Item during -Force extraction since they do not indicate a real extraction failure.
Consider using a fresh/ephemeral workspace per job on self-hosted Windows runners for this job, or add an explicit workspace-cleanup step before artifact download/extraction.
Re-run the failed 'GPU unit tests' job; this is a transient runner-state issue unrelated to the PR changes.
prevention_strategies: Always clear or recreate the destination directory before Expand-Archive -Force on persistent self-hosted runners rather than depending on its internal reconciliation of previously-extracted files, since that reconciliation can fail if the runner's filesystem state has drifted between jobs (partial cleanups, crashed previous runs, manual intervention, or disk issues).
historical_context: A related but distinct recurring pattern (signature_hash 95bb23aa2ed8a84d, 10 occurrences) also affects the 'GPU unit tests' / Extract OpenVINO packages step on Windows self-hosted runners, but with a different root cause: Remove-Item failing with UnauthorizedAccessException because tbb12.dll is locked by another process (file-lock contention), not PathNotFound (missing file). No prior investigation of this specific PathNotFound/missing-license-file signature was found in the pattern database; this is the first recorded occurrence.
